response: No, computerised tomography (CT) cannot completely replace bone scintigraphy in detecting bone metastases from breast cancer. While CT scans can detect bone metastases, bone scintigraphy is more sensitive in detecting early metastatic disease, particularly in the bone marrow, due to its ability to identify areas of increased bone turnover. However, CT scans can provide more detailed information about the structure and extent of bone lesions, making it a useful complementary tool in the diagnosis and management of bone metastases from breast cancer.
